winAmount.help: How many rounds a team has to win to take the match. A **Kot** is worth more than one, so a match can be won in fewer rounds than this number.

trickTarget.title: Tricks to win a round
trickTarget.help: How many of the thirteen tricks a team has to take to win the round. Seven is the classic majority; a lower number ends each round sooner.

trumpTime.title: Trump Call Time
trumpTime.help: How long the Hakem gets to name the trump suit. If the clock runs out, their longest suit is called for them.

help.double: 'Kot' makes a 7-0 round worth two points instead of one.
help.hakemKot: 'Kot & Hakem Kot' also makes sweeping the Hakem's own team worth three points.
help.off: 'Disabled' scores every round won as a single point, however one-sided it was.

hakemSelection.title: Picking the first Hakem
hakemSelection.help: How the very first trump caller is found. Every round after that follows the retention rule below.

rules.title: Rules
description: Hokm is played by four people in two teams of two, with partners sitting opposite each other. Every card of a standard 52-card deck is dealt, so everybody holds thirteen.
One player is the **Hakem**. They see their first cards before anybody else and name the **trump** suit that beats every other suit for the rest of the round.

trump.title: Trump and following suit
description: The Hakem leads the first trick. Everybody else has to **follow suit** if they can; only a player holding none of the suit that was led may play something else.
The highest trump played takes the trick. If nobody trumped it, the highest card of the suit that was led wins. Aces are high.

tricks.title: Taking tricks
description: Whoever takes a trick leads the next one, so winning it also means choosing what everybody has to follow next.
The first team to take **seven** tricks wins the round — the rest of the cards are not played out.

scoring.title: Scoring
description: Each round won is worth a point, and the first team to seven points wins the match. Taking all seven tricks is a **Kot**, and is worth two.
The Hakem stays Hakem while their team keeps winning; the moment they lose a round, the call passes to the player on their right.

bots.title: Bots
description: Easy bots play any card the rules allow. Normal bots read the trick in front of them: they stay out of a partner's winning trick and take the rest as cheaply as they can.

Hard bots count the cards. They remember which suits you have run out of, which high cards are gone, and which suits you have chosen to lead — so leading a suit at your partner twice is something they will answer.
